_README: The traffic allowances the bandwidth tracker measures against.
This is a configuration file, not a measurement, and the tracker treats it that
way: every window carries who confirmed it and when, and the operations page
prints that provenance next to the number. There is deliberately no fallback
constant anywhere in ops/bandwidth.py -- if this file is missing, the page says
the allowance is unknown rather than inventing one, because an allowance the
code made up would look exactly like one Sean confirmed.
A window with no effectiveFrom is ANNOUNCED, not in force. It is displayed so
an operator can see what is coming, and it is never used in any arithmetic.
When Sean's fibre install completes, set its effectiveFrom to the date the new
plan starts and the page follows on the next run -- no code change.
unlimited:true means there is no ceiling. Every percentage-of-allowance figure
on the page becomes 'no ceiling' rather than a division by zero.
counts: which DIRECTION the allowance bills. This field is load-bearing. The
VPS allowance is egress-only, so the bigmem-to-VPS publish traffic -- which is
ingress at the VPS -- does not touch it at all. Getting this wrong would have
sent Sean optimising the wrong number.

home.label: Sean's home internet (bigmem's connection)
home.sourceNote: Sean confirmed 1.25 TB/month on 2026-08-08. The billing RESET DAY has not been confirmed; the tracker assumes the calendar month (UTC) and says so.

windows.note: 1.25 TB/month. Confirmed by Sean 2026-08-08, superseding a 2 TB figure given earlier from memory.

T-Mobile fibre, unlimited. Sean announced this on 2026-08-08 as 'later this week'. NOT IN FORCE: no start date has been recorded, so the tracker is still measuring against 1.25 TB. Set effectiveFrom to the install date to switch.

vps.label: Hetzner CPX31, Ashburn (openclaw-ash-1)
vps.sourceNote: 3 TB egress, confirmed by Sean 2026-08-08 and corroborated the same day against Hetzner's own documentation: the Cloud billing FAQ (docs.hetzner.com/cloud/billing/faq/) states 'We only bill for outgoing traffic. Incoming and internal traffic is free', and Hetzner's cloud_data.json shows CPX31 at ASH1 (Ashburn) with 3 TB included and EUR 1.00/USD 1.20 per additional TB. So the bigmem-to-VPS publish traffic, which is ingress here, does not consume this allowance -- only bytes served to visitors do. NOT verified per-server: whether this particular server was grandfathered onto a larger allowance can only be settled by GET /v1/servers included_traffic on the Hetzner API, which has not been run.

windows.note: 3 TB/month of EGRESS. Confirmed by Sean 2026-08-08.
